true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate self.downsize method shadows earlier definition

Two class methods named self.downsize are defined back-to-back: one with signature (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) on lines 145-147 and another with signature (from, to, dimensions, opts) on lines 149-151. In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first; the four-arg overload becomes dead code that is never reachable. The unused definition is misleading and will silently break any other caller that still passes separate width/height integers (those calls would now misroute 200 into the opts hash and raise NoMethodError on opts[:allow_animation]). The dead method should be deleted so only the (from, to, dimensions, opts) form remains.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side file-size limit hardcoded to 10 MB and no longer uses SiteSettings

validateUploadedFile previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and displayErrorForUpload read `SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`). The PR replaces both with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. The server-side controller still uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (now with an auto-downsize step, but a server-enforced ceiling remains). This decouples client and server validation: an admin who lowers max_image_size_kb below 10 MB will see uploads rejected on the server with a generic 413, while the browser still claims files up to 10 MB are valid; raising max_image_size_kb above 10 MB will not relax the client-side cap. The previous site-setting based values should be restored, or the server limit should also be aligned with 10 MB.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Passing '80%' to gifsicle --resize-fit will fail for animated GIFs

The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). The animated branch in resize_instructions_animated assembles `gifsicle <from> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <to>`. gifsicle's --resize-fit expects pixel dimensions of the form WxH; it does not accept a percentage. When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the uploaded image is a GIF, this command will either be rejected by gifsicle or produce no useful output, so the downsize loop's exit-condition (tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes) will never become false and the GIF will be uploaded unmodified (and likely over the size limit).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize loop does not verify the file is now within the size limit

The retry loop only checks `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` before each iteration; if OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (e.g. convert/gifsicle fails, source is unsupported, or the file just can't be compressed enough at 80% scale for five attempts), the loop still exits with attempt reaching 0. The code then unconditionally calls Upload.create_for with `tempfile.size` and creates an Upload record whose underlying file exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. There is no fallback to reject the upload, no log line, and the user gets no error. The loop should re-check size after the downsize call (e.g. re-stat the file) and treat remaining-oversize as an error returned to the caller.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is blank

`before_validation` unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')`. If the attribute is nil or was never assigned (e.g. a Fabricator without a `host:`, or a controller call that omits the param), `sub!` is invoked on nil and raises `NoMethodError`, instead of being reported as a 422 validation error. Add `validates_presence_of :host`, guard the `sub!` (e.g. `self.host = (self.host || '').sub(...)` then assign back), and the model-level presence validation will then return clean errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy crash when EmbeddableHost is missing

`update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then calls `save_host(host)`, which immediately invokes `host.host = ...` on nil. `destroy` does `host.destroy` on nil. Any PUT/DELETE to `/admin/embeddable_hosts/<bogus-id>` raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Guard the lookup with `host || (raise Discourse::NotFound)` (or `head :not_found`) before use.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration skips model validations during data backfill

The backfill INSERTs hosts directly via `execute`, bypassing `validates_format_of :host` and the `before_validation` normalization (http(s):// and trailing-path stripping). Any existing entries containing `http://`, a trailing path, or characters outside `[a-z0-9\-\.]` are reproduced verbatim, then fail format validation when an admin later edits them. Either run the same normalization in SQL inside the migration or call `EmbeddableHost.create!(host: h, category_id: category_id, skip_validation: false)` (or use the model's `before_validation` to clean values before insertion).

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
SQL injection in data migration

The migration string-interpolates the per-line host value directly into an INSERT statement: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)`. The `h` strings come from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which an admin controls. The model-level `validates_format_of :host` does NOT run during this raw INSERT, so values like `'); DROP TABLE users; --` would be inserted verbatim and could corrupt or destroy the database. Use parameterized SQL (e.g. `execute("INSERT ... VALUES (?, ?, ...)", h, category_id)`) or instantiate `EmbeddableHost.new(host: h, category_id: category_id).save(validate: false)` so input is escaped.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration raises NoMethodError when embed_category was never set

The first query `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")` returns zero rows when the `embed_category` site setting was never populated (which is the common case for fresh installs and for any install that doesn't use embedding). The code then does `...[0]['id'].to_i`, which throws `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the migration, leaving the DB in a half-migrated state. Guard the lookup (e.g. check `result.cmd_tuples > 0` before indexing) and fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when the join yields nothing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Admin embedding page cannot render existing embeddable_hosts

`EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids`, which only emits `embeddable_host_ids: [..]` on the parent and does NOT include the `embeddable_hosts` collection in the payload root. On the client, `store._hydrateEmbedded` then looks up each ID via `_lookupSubType('embeddable_host', ...)` which depends on `root['embeddable_hosts']` existing, finds nothing, and assigns `embedding.embeddable_hosts = [undefined, undefined, undefined]`. The Handlebars `{{#each embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` iterates those undefined entries and crashes the component when it dereferences `host.isNew` / `host.host`. As a result the page can't display any pre-existing hosts. Either include the `embeddable_hosts` collection in the response root (e.g. embed: :objects, or have the route do a separate `findAll('embeddable-host')`), or have the serializer/hydration fall back to a freshly-fetched list.

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController has no CRUD tests

The only spec checks class inheritance. There is no coverage for `create`/`update`/`destroy`, no test verifying that a blank `host` is rejected (regression risk on the `before_validation`/presence gap), no test that the `category_id` falls back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, and no test that unknown IDs return 404. Add specs covering at least: create with valid params, create with blank/invalid host returning 422, update changing both fields, destroy with missing id returning 404, and authorization for non-admin staff.

Admin::EmbeddingController has no behavioural tests

The only spec for `Admin::EmbeddingController` checks that it is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. The new admin embedding page is the centrepiece of this PR: GET should require staff and return a serialized embedding with its hosts, PUT should round-trip the (no-op) update. Without at least one happy-path and one unauthorized request test, regressions in routing, the serializer, or the staff-only filter will go unnoticed.

Embedded topic silently created with wrong/nil category when host lookup fails

`eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` returns false (not nil) when no host matches, and `try(:category_id)` then yields `nil`. The PostCreator is called with `category: nil`, which combined with `SiteSetting.allow_uncategorized_topics = false` and the Topic validates produce behaviour that diverges from the previous behaviour (`SiteSetting.embed_category`, which was always set or nil). Previously it was obvious when there was no configured category; now import can succeed silently or fail in `changed_to_category`, with no error surfaced to the caller. Consider raising or returning nil explicitly when `eh` is false so the caller knows the URL didn't match a configured host and the topic was not created in the expected category.

No uniqueness constraint on EmbeddableHost.host

Neither the model nor the migration enforce uniqueness on `host`. Multiple admins can create duplicate rows for the same site, leaving stale rows that survive deletion and confuse the host picker. Add `validates :host, presence: true, uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false }` on the model and `add_index :embeddable_hosts, :host, unique: true` (case-insensitive) in the migration so race conditions can't create duplicates.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist

The unsubscribe action does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then unconditionally calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!`. For any user who has not previously visited/read the topic (or whose topic_users row was deleted) there is no TopicUser row and `find_by` returns nil, so the first comparison raises NoMethodError on nil and the user sees a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. New users on a topic they have never opened will hit this on the very first click from the email. The action should use `TopicUser.find_or_create_by(...)` (or the existing `TopicUser.change` helper which already creates the row on miss) and otherwise guard against nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Misspelled property leaks to template handlebars

The CP is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i' after Notific). The template (`templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) refers to it as `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` so it works, but the misspelling will bite anyone who tries to grep, rename, or reuse it, and Ember will warn about unknown handlebars bindings the moment either side is corrected. Rename to `stopNotificationsText` and update the template accordingly.

false_positives.candidate: GET-based state change with no auth token enables CSRF unsubscribe The unsubscribe endpoint is GET-only and the URL it generates (`{base}/t/{slug}/{id}/unsubscribe`) contains no per-user authentication token, unlike Discourse's other email-triggered endpoints (e.g. `email/unsubscribe/:key`, `users/password-reset/:token`, `users/activate-account/:token`). Any third-party site can force a logged-in Discourse user to be unsubscribed/muted from any topic simply by referencing the URL (e.g. as an ``, hidden link, or redirect). Once the user lands on it, `tu.save!` mutates their notification level with no confirm step. The action should either be POST/PUT (so Rails' CSRF token applies) or the link in the email should carry a signed/email-token like the existing global unsubscribe (`email#unsubscribe`) does.

New unsubscribe behavior is not actually asserted

The diff only adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the existing `message_with_unsubscribe` let-block, but no expectation is added that this URL ends up in the rendered body. The "unsubscribe link" context only checks that the user preferences URL appears; there is no test asserting that `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the `unsubscribe_link` i18n key and surfaces in the body/html_part. Given the i18n string was changed and the unsubscribe_url plumbing is brand new, a regression here would silently produce emails with the global-preferences-only footer again.

No controller spec for the new unsubscribe action

There is no topics_controller_spec coverage for the new `unsubscribe` action: nil-TopicUser case, slug mismatch redirect, the regular->muted vs tracking/watching->regular branch, permission denial, and that the rendered view is `topics/show`. Combined with the silent `tu.save!` and the fact that this action is the entry point for every per-topic unsubscribe email, a regression here will only be caught in production.

No explicit guardian check before mutating state

Before doing `tu.save!` the controller relies on `TopicView.new` raising to deny access, but there is no explicit `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or equivalent). If `TopicView.new` ever stops raising for some category/PM edge case, or if a later refactor changes that, the action will happily downgrade a TopicUser row for a topic the user is not entitled to interact with. Add an explicit guardian check (matching the pattern used by `clear_pin`/`re_pin`/`mute` in the same controller) before mutating user state.

mailing_list_notify omits unsubscribe_url, breaking the feature for mailing-list users

`send_notification_email` is shared between the per-user notification path and `mailing_list_notify`, but `mailing_list_notify` (lines 146-159) builds its opts hash without `unsubscribe_url:` while the other callers now pass `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`. As a result users in mailing-list mode still get the old footer with only the global preferences link and no per-topic unsubscribe link, which is inconsistent with the stated goal of this PR and means the new i18n text "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})" is never shown for these emails.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email validation does a DB write on every blocked-email hit

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` is invoked from `validate_each`, which runs on every user save when the email changes. Each call performs a SELECT plus an UPDATE to track statistics. That makes a previously pure read-side validation write to the DB and, combined with the read-modify-write race above, turns user signup into a small thundering herd against `blocked_emails`. Consider tracking match stats out-of-band (background job, or only when not blocked by the domain check), or at minimum batching the write.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email is not case-normalized; admin and signup inputs must match exactly

Both the model and the migration store `email` verbatim (case-sensitive unique index). The new validator compares it case-sensitively, and User#email is set from `params[:email]` without `Email.downcase`, so `Bad@Spam.com` (admin entry) and `bad@spam.com` (signup) are treated as different addresses. A blocklist entry that looks correct in the admin UI can be bypassed by submitting the same address with different casing, or with surrounding whitespace. Normalize via `before_validation` (e.g. `self.email = Email.downcase(email.to_s.strip)`) and consider a case-insensitive index so this can't be bypassed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Whitelist/blacklist paths were moved from User but have no test coverage

The EmailValidator now owns the entire domain whitelist/blacklist logic that previously lived in `User#email_validator`, but the spec only covers the BlockedEmail branch. A regression in the regex construction (e.g. `setting.gsub('.', '\.')` with a comma-separated list — currently `@(gmail\.com,foo\.bar)`, which only matches the literal string `gmail.com,foo.bar`, not either domain) would not be caught. Add specs covering: whitelist allows/disallows, blacklist allows/disallows, comma-separated domains, interaction with BlockedEmail (whitelist fail vs block list), and that `record.errors[:email]` contains the expected key.

record.save runs validations/callbacks for a counter update

Calling `record.save` triggers the full ActiveRecord lifecycle (validations including `uniqueness`, callbacks) every time an email is checked, just to bump a counter. If a uniqueness race loses, the in-memory `record` is still returned as truthy in `should_block?`, so the user is blocked while the match counter was never persisted, and the exception is silently swallowed. For pure-statistic writes, use `update_columns`/`update_all` so the outcome isn't tied to a `save` succeeding.

rejectedEmails.contains is case-sensitive, allowing easy bypass of client-side block

`this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email)` does a strict string compare. After the server rejects `Bad@Spam.com`, that exact string is pushed. The user can then re-enter `bad@spam.com` (or add a space); the client validation passes, they resubmit, and only then learn from the server it's blocked. The UX promise of this PR — instant feedback for blocked emails — is broken. Normalize both sides (e.g. `email.toLowerCase()`) before pushing into `rejectedEmails` and before the contains check.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf instead of a real origin comparison

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` only confirms that e.origin appears as a substring of discourseUrl. Any e.origin that is a substring of whatever `discourseUrl` is configured to (including future paths/queries/cached redirects) will pass the gate and be allowed to set `iframe.height` or drive other future message handlers. Use `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin` (or compare parsed origins via the postMessage API's own origin field) so the handler accepts only the configured Discourse origin.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Embed URL injected raw into HTML, enabling XSS in the rendered embed view The embed URL is interpolated unescaped into both the href attribute and the link text via I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}"). Imported posts are persisted with cook_method = :raw_html and the embed view renders their HTML through `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so the appended markup is emitted verbatim into the discourse origin. An embed URL containing a single quote, a newline, an `on*=` payload, or a `javascript:` scheme (originating from any RSS item, from a CMS at SiteSetting.embeddable_host, or from any direct caller of TopicEmbed.import) breaks out of the `` attribute and runs attacker-supplied HTML/JS. The call also mutates the caller's `contents` string in place via `<<`, which can break frozen-string inputs and corrupts the caller's data. Use Rails' link_to(url) (or html_escape) and build the suffix into a separate String instead of mutating `contents`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
<%- end if %> is a SyntaxError in Ruby ERB and will prevent the embed view from rendering

Line 6 closes the first if/else block with `  <%- end if %>`. Inside ERB that compiles to the literal Ruby `end if`, whose `if` modifier requires a condition expression. With no condition following `if`, Ruby's parser raises a SyntaxError the first time the view is compiled, so any request that reaches `best.html.erb` (i.e., any embedded topic that has been imported) will blow up instead of rendering. The other if/else in this same file (lines 11, 22, 29) closes with plain `<%- end %>`, confirming that this is a stray ` if` typo. Replace with `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed job aborts the entire hourly run on the first item or network failure

Inside the `rss.items.each` loop, `i.content.scrub` raises on a nil/Non-String item content, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` raises on any transient network or HTTP error, and `TopicEmbed.import` raises on URL-regex mismatch or Nokogiri errors from `absolutize_urls`. Combined with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, one malformed item or one bad network response silently drops every subsequent item in the feed until the next hourly cron — and the exceptions are lost because the `feed_polling_enabled?` guard never runs around the loop. Wrap each item (and the open/parse) in begin/rescue, validate i.link/i.id/i.title/i.content up front, and log per-item errors so a single bad entry does not poison the entire run.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
request.referer is interpolated into a JS context without j/JS escaping

`parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` relies on Rails default HTML escaping inside a JavaScript string literal. While `'` happens to be escaped in a way that is inert inside a `<script>` block today, the correct helper for a value going into a JS string literal is `j request.referer` (or escaping explicitly for targetOrigin). The embed controller deliberately lets attacker-controllable URLs reach the referer header, so passing that value to postMessage's targetOrigin should be JS-escaped so that backslashes/control bytes produced by a hostile header cannot break the JS string or smuggle a different targetOrigin.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Throttle uses non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE, which can leak a permanent key

`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` leaves a brief window in which the key exists with no TTL. If the second command is lost (network blip, sidekiq preemption, Redis failover) the key has no expiry and permanently blocks retrievals for that URL. Use the atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` form instead.

TopicEmbed.import_remote (external URL fetch + ruby-readability) is not exercised

import_remote performs `open(url).read`, runs ruby-readability with the specific tags/attributes allowlist, and forwards the result into import. It is the highest-risk entry point in this PR (SSRF surface, hang on slow hosts, content that ends up as raw_html posts) and is reachable from both TopicRetriever#fetch_http and the disqus.thor import task. The new spec only covers import(), so any regression in the allowlist, the host contract, or the read/open behaviour would slip through.

X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a recognized directive

The action unconditionally sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. The only valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and the deprecated ALLOW-FROM <uri>. Browsers will silently ignore "ALLOWALL" and fall back to their default framing policy, so unless an equivalent Content-Security-Policy `frame-ancestors *` is set, the very framing that the embed feature was built to enable will be blocked in modern browsers. Use CSP `frame-ancestors *` (or remove this header and rely on CSP) instead.

feed_key helper is dead code

The class defines `feed_key` (computing `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) but never references it. Either wire it into the poll path (e.g., a per-feed HTTP If-Modified-Since/last-modified check, or a rate-limit key to avoid re-importing unchanged items) or remove the unused method to avoid the impression that per-feed change detection exists.

poll_feed body (RSS item iteration, normalisation, TopicEmbed.import integration) is uncovered

The new spec only verifies the three guard conditions in execute() (feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url present, embed_by_username present). The actual poll_feed body that parses the feed, falls back from i.link to i.id, runs CGI.unescapeHTML + i.content.scrub, and calls TopicEmbed.import per item is the section this review flagged as fragile (nil item fields, scrub failures, regex mismatch on id fallback) and is not tested at all.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin

The new `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid CSS property. The only IE10-prefixed property for alignment is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on line 120). The invalid `-ms-align-items` declaration is silently ignored by browsers and is dead CSS.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalid -moz-inline-box value in inline-flex mixin

The new `inline-flex` mixin emits `display: -moz-inline-box;`, but Firefox never implemented an inline variant of its legacy `-moz-box` model — only the block-level `-moz-box` existed. true_positives.matched_candidate:
ensure_loaded! has a data race on @loaded_locales

ensure_loaded! initializes @loaded_locales ||= [] outside any mutex and then calls load_locale, which itself protects only the body via LOAD_MUTEX. Two threads that race on the first call can each observe @loaded_locales as nil, create separate Array instances, and the last write wins. Whichever instance is no longer referenced loses its additions, so subsequent calls into ensure_loaded!/load_locale can re-load already-loaded locales. The mutex currently held only by load_locale is not sufficient because @loaded_locales may flip between two arrays mid-flight. Initialize the ivar under the same LOAD_MUTEX (or use a Set guarded by the mutex) so the @loaded_locales reference itself is stable.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fallback chain mixes String and Symbol locales

set_locale in application_controller.rb assigns I18n.locale from current_user.effective_locale or SiteSetting.default_locale, which return String values in Discourse. The fallback chain is [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en], so the chain can contain a String like 'fr' alongside Symbols :en. Array#uniq does not deduplicate values of different types, so 'en' and :en would both end up in the chain and load_locale would add both to @loaded_locales in translate_accelerator.rb. This results in wasted reloads and risks comparison surprises in i18n internals or third-party code. Coerce locale to a Symbol (e.g. locale.to_sym) so the chain is uniformly typed.

The two places previously disagreed in subtle ways and a future engineer may add the Rails-style line back, double-enabling the Fallbacks module, or assume the initializer is the only source of truth. Leave a one-line note in each environment file pointing at the initializer, or document the migration in the initializer itself.

FallbackLocaleList inherits Hash but only overrides []

FallbackLocaleList < Hash redefines only the [] method. All other methods of I18n::Locale::Fallbacks that callers may rely on (e.g. defaults, defaults=, compute, map, each over configured fallbacks, []=) are left as plain Hash methods that operate on an always-empty Hash. Any plugin or piece of code that does I18n.fallbacks[:zh_TW] = [:zh_TW, :zh_CN, :en] will silently be ignored because lookup always goes through the overridden []. Methods like I18n.fallbacks.defaults will raise NoMethodError. Either stop inheriting Hash or implement the full Locale::Fallbacks contract so that per-locale configuration and other API consumers are not broken.

The PR introduces a new FallbackLocaleList class, a custom I18n.fallbacks implementation, the new I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! method, and a new I18n.ensure_loaded! method on the freedom patch. None of these changes have accompanying specs. There is no coverage verifying: that the fallback chain order is correct for users vs anonymous requests, that I18n.locale changes between requests trigger reloads, that SiteSetting.default_locale is honored as a fallback, that missing keys in a non-English locale correctly fall back to English, or that ensure_loaded! is idempotent. The PR description 'Test 9' does not indicate tests are present anywhere.

ensure_loaded! allocates per request in a before_filter

set_locale runs as a before_filter on every request, and the new line invokes I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which calls self[I18n.locale] and allocates a new Array every time, then iterates it calling I18n.ensure_loaded! for each fallback locale. KeyError on spans missing end_timestamp_precise

The new code uses `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` with subscript access, while every other optional field in the same Span constructor (parent_span_id, is_remote) uses `.get()`. Any span payload already buffered in the ingest-spans Kafka topic (or coming from a producer that has not yet been upgraded) that lacks this key will raise KeyError and crash the consumer batch. Use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise")` (or fall back to a sentinel such as 0.0) for forward compatibility with in-flight messages.

OptimizedCursorPaginator added with no test coverage

OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-copy of BasePaginator.get_result with a security-relevant behavior change (allowing negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features=True`). It is wired into the audit-logs endpoint and gated only by `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but there are zero tests for the class itself, for `enable_advanced_features=True` path, for negative offsets, or for the auditlog endpoint's new `optimized_pagination=true` branch. A paginator that silently changes the cursor contract for admins deserves its own tests in tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py and tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py.

Pre-existing typo order_b still present in BasePaginator.build_queryset

In `BasePaginator.build_queryset` the branch that flips `-key` ordering back to ascending writes `queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by)` — `order_b` is not an attribute of `Query` (the correct attribute is `order_by`). As a result, the reversed ordering is silently dropped and the queryset is left ordered by `-key` even though the code intended `+key`. This is in the same file the diff touches and is exercised by every caller using a descending order_by with a `is_prev=True` cursor that has a cursor value. It must be fixed before this PR lands; the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` inherits from `BasePaginator` and inherits the bug.

max_segment_spans protection silently removed from flush path

`_load_segment_data` previously guarded against runaway segments by deleting any key whose accumulated span count exceeded `self.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and emitting the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric. The diff deletes that branch entirely and the constructor parameter `max_segment_spans` is now dead — no code reads it. The new in-Lua `zpopmin` eviction runs on the insert path, but it does not protect against (a) segments populated before this rollout, (b) sets that exceed 1000 entries between two insert calls, or (c) the case where `zcard(set_key)` after `zunionstore` returns 0 because both source sets were empty (so eviction is skipped even though `zcard` afterward would still report >1000). Without the flush-time guard a single oversized segment will now be loaded into memory and serialized, which is exactly what the old check prevented.

zpopmin eviction key is not actually oldest spans

Eviction uses `zpopmin` against `end_timestamp_precise` scores. When many spans in a segment share the same `end_timestamp_precise` (which is the common case for spans belonging to the same transaction), Redis sorted-set ordering for ties is lexicographic on the member bytes, i.e. on the JSON payload. The "evict oldest" policy therefore degenerates to "evict whichever serialized payload sorts first," which is essentially arbitrary and may preferentially drop small/different payloads. The score should include a deterministic tiebreaker (e.g. span_id) so eviction order is reproducible.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache key uses hash() of project_ids tuple

The cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. While `hash(int)` is deterministic in CPython, mixing `hash()` of a derived structure into a cache key is fragile (it depends on tuple-hash internals and any future changes to them) and produces opaque keys that are hard to inspect/grep in Redis. A deterministic, explicit key like `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{','.join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))}"` (or a sha1 prefix) would be safer, debuggable, and immune to future interpreter changes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

false_positives.candidate:
Error message wording regression adjacent to top_events validation

The diff changes the response message from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. The new wording is grammatically cleaner, but it is bundled into a commit titled `feat(upsampling)` with no mention of an API/UX message change. Because this is a public 400 response body on `organization-events-stats`, any client that does an exact-string match on this `detail` value (e.g. localised tooling) will break. The change should either be split into its own commit or called out in the description.

Stale upsampling eligibility cache has no invalidation hook

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the all-projects-in-allowlist result for 60 seconds, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided but never called from anywhere in the diff (no admin signal, option listener, or tests cover invalidation). If a project is added to or removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, requests for the next minute will continue to use the previous decision. In the worst case (allowlist shrinks while cache still says eligible) the endpoint will issue `sum(sample_weight)` queries for projects that no longer guarantee non-null `sample_weight`, potentially producing the silent undercount called out above. There should be an explicit invalidation call (or a much shorter TTL, or no cache) wired up before merging.

Tests do not cover caching, invalidation, aliased count(), or NULL sample_weight

The new test file covers the allowlist membership, the basic `count()` transform, the `event.type:error` substring check, and the dataset dispatch, but misses the most failure-prone paths: (1) `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is never tested, so the cache key construction (`hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`), cache-hit fast path, and 60s TTL behaviour are entirely uncovered; (2) `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` is never given aliased inputs (`count() as my_count`) so the limitation called out above is not pinned by a test; (3) there is no test asserting behaviour when a project in the allowlist emits events without `sample_weight`. Adding at least one cache-hit/miss test and an aliased-count test would prevent the cache and transform edge cases from regressing unnoticed.

Unnecessary try/except around safe dict lookups

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps the chained `.get(...).get(...).get(...)` in a `try/except Exception: pass` and the `float(...)` conversion in another one. `dict.get` cannot raise for missing keys, and a malformed `client_sample_rate` string is the only realistic failure mode, which the second `try` already handles. The first try/except hides real bugs (e.g. `AttributeError` from a malformed contexts payload) and should be removed; only the `float()` conversion needs to be defensive.

_is_error_focused_query uses substring match on query string

`_is_error_focused_query` decides based on `"event.type:error" in query`. The check is a raw substring match, so queries like `event.type:error_handled` (if such an alias is ever introduced) or any token that begins with `event.type:error` would be treated as error-focused and force the upsampled transformation on a dataset that may include non-error rows. A safer check parses the query tokens (e.g. via `event_search.parse_search_query`) and inspects the actual `event.type` value rather than doing a substring `in`.

setUp reassigns self.user after login_as, breaking auth identity

In `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, the test calls `self.login_as(user=self.user)` with the user that `APITestCase.setUp` created, then immediately overwrites `self.user = self.create_user()`. From that point on, `self.user` no longer refers to the authenticated user, and any tag, audit log entry, or future test that reads `self.user` will silently use the wrong identity. In particular the events stored right below use `self.user.email` / `self.user2.email` as the `sentry:user` tag, which means the test is asserting counts against events whose owner does not match the calling API user; if any later assertion (or downstream test) compares user identity this will fail.

sum(sample_weight) silently drops NULL sample_weight rows

`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` which is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. ClickHouse/SnQL `sum` ignores NULL arguments entirely, so any allowlisted-project event that has `sample_weight IS NULL` is silently omitted from the result, undercounting errors. The comment claims the schema guarantees `sample_weight` is non-null for allowlisted projects, but nothing in this helper (or in `discover.py`) enforces or even validates that invariant. There should be at minimum a guard that rejects the transformation (or coalesces `sample_weight` to a fallback) when the project list could contain NULL-weight events, otherwise dashboards/alerts that switch to upsampled counts will report numbers lower than the truth with no warning.

transform only matches literal count(), misses aliased and surrounded variants

`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` compares `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`. This single-equality test misses common variants that should still be upsampled: `count() as my_count`, `count() AS errors`, `count("id")` (counting a specific column), or `count()` surrounded by extra inner whitespace. As a result, a column written as `count() as count` (with explicit alias) will be passed through unchanged while the same column written as `count()` will be replaced with `upsampled_count() as count`, giving two clients querying the same metric different aggregations. The transform should at least recognise `count()` with a trailing `as <alias>` clause.

upsampled_count SnQLFunction not marked private

The newly added `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, unlike the surrounding private helpers (e.g. `thing_expression`, `count_at_least`). Without that flag the function becomes part of the user-exposed SnQL/Discover function surface, so end users could write `upsampled_count()` in their own queries. The function is only meaningful in conjunction with the project allowlist/sampling-rate pipeline, and emits `sum(sample_weight)` which has different semantics (and potential NULL-handling) from `count()`. Users invoking it directly outside of `organization_events_stats` will get counts that silently diverge from what they expect.

false_positives.candidate:
Broad except in get_environment_info swallows all errors silently

`get_environment_info` catches a bare `Exception` and only logs at info level via `logger.info(...)`. Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'

The corresponding project option default in `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (line 205) was also changed. This is a user-facing behavior change that should be called out explicitly in the PR description and potentially coordinated with documentation/release notes, as existing projects that rely on the default will not be affected, but new projects will have a different experience.

Feedback separator changed from list format to raw join

The separator for joining feedback entries changed from `"
".join(f"- {msg}" for msg in feedbacks)` (which produced a bulleted list) to `"
------
".join(feedbacks)` (which produces raw separator-delimited entries). This is a significant change in how feedback is presented to the LLM. If any feedback message contains the substring `------`, it could be confused with a separator. Additionally, the new format doesn't provide visual structure (no bullet points), which may affect LLM summarization quality. This should be tested to ensure the LLM still produces good summaries with the new format.

dcg_to_slow_conditions source changed from dcg_to_groups.keys() to dcg_ids

Previously, `get_condition_query_groups` computed `dcg_to_slow_conditions` from `list(event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys())`, while `get_groups_to_fire` computed it from `list(event_data.dcg_ids)`. true_positives.golden_comment: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Disable endpoint logs a 'backup code login' error

The console.error inside the backup-code branch logs 'Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.' This handler lives at /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable, not a login endpoint. Operators reading server logs during a disable incident will be misled into believing a login attempt failed. true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Race condition lets a backup code be reused

The backup-code consumption path in authorize() reads user.backupCodes, decrypts it with JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)), nulls the matched slot, re-encrypts, and writes the result back via prisma.user.update with no atomicity guard. Two concurrent requests submitting different valid backup codes both read the same pre-image, each null a different index in their local copy, and whichever update commits last overwrites the other writer's null — restoring the slot the first request consumed. Consequence: a backup code can be used more than once, breaking the one-time-use guarantee the PR explicitly relies on (see the comment 'delete verified backup code and re-encrypt remaining'). Fix by making the update atomic, e.g. wrap read+write in prisma.$transaction, or include the expected pre-image in the WHERE clause so the second writer is rejected.

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-codes Blob URL is never revoked when the modal closes

handleSetup calls URL.createObjectURL(textBlob) to produce the download link for the user's plaintext backup codes and stores it in backupCodesUrl. There is no URL.revokeObjectURL call when the modal closes — resetState() only clears password, errorMessage, and step, and the component has no unmount cleanup. The Blob keeps the user's plaintext backup codes alive in memory until either the next successful setup (which revokes the previous URL) or the page is unloaded. Revoke the URL inside resetState and in a useEffect cleanup that runs on unmount.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Backup-code login and disable flows are not tested

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

`const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` The `.find` predicate requires `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`; since we are in the falsy branch of the ternary this becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, never true. BaseCalendarService.createEvent does not match new Calendar interface signature

The Calendar interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, but this class still implements `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with no `credentialId` parameter. This is a TypeScript contract violation for any app that extends BaseCalendarService (e.g. caldav-style providers), and at runtime this implementation does not filter `event.destinationCalendar` by credential, so on a collective event whose first entry is a Google/Lark calendar it will request the wrong external id and likely fail.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancellation only includes a single destination calendar, losing team calendars

The CalendarEvent built here wraps only `bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar` or the user destination in a single-element array and never collects other team hosts' destinations. handleNewBooking now aggregates host destination calendars into a multi-element array for new bookings; cancellation must do the same or cancellations on collective events will leak the secondary calendars (their events still exist because `deleteEvent` is called per reference, but emails/webhooks reflect only one calendar and the symmetry between create and cancel is broken).

Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar regardless of credential

EventManager.create iterates over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` to drive the per-host booking. Lark's createEvent ignores the credential/externalId it was given and falls back to `event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (first element). In a collective event whose first destination belongs to a Google host, Lark will be asked to create the event under that Google external id and the request will fail or write to the wrong calendar.

Main-host external id reused as organizer email even when event is created on another host's calendar

`email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email,` is taken from the FIRST destination calendar (the main host's calendar), but the actual insertion below happens on the calendar returned by `destinationCalendar?.find(c => c.credentialId === credentialId)`, which may be a different host. As a result, when a non-main host's Google calendar is the target, the organizer entry in that calendar's event will be the main host's externalId/email instead of the true calendar owner's.

Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and may address the wrong calendar

Same pattern as Lark: the new Calendar interface and EventManager pass `credentialId` and `destination.externalId`, but Office365's implementation just takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event the first destination is typically the main host's calendar (e.g. Google), so the Office365 call would attempt `https://graph.microsoft.com/.../calendars/<google-external-id>/events` and fail.

PR makes no new tests for the multi-host collective booking flow it claims to fix

The change converts `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and rewires creation/cancellation across many files, fixing #7754 (collective events with multiple destination calendars per host). The PR description itself notes 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective'. The existing `webhook.e2e.ts` update only changes the expected `destinationCalendar` literal in a single webhook assertion, which does not exercise the new per-host creation or per-host cancellation flow.

When merging bookings, only first calendar reference of the old booking is deleted

`const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` returns at most one reference. For a collective reschedule that produced multiple calendar references on the old booking, only the first one will be deleted on its provider. The remaining calendar events stay on the user's calendar and effectively become orphans.

destinationCalendar built without user.destinationCalendar fallback, inconsistent with other handlers

All sibling handlers (confirm, cancelBooking, editLocation, handleNewBooking, deleteCredential, paypal/stripe webhooks, bookingReminder) fall back to `user.destinationCalendar` when `booking.destinationCalendar` is null. This handler does not, so for users whose only destinationCalendar lives on the user (not the booking), the request-reschedule flow will silently go through with `destinationCalendar: []`, which EventManager.create interprets as 'no destination'.

loadUsers try/catch swallows programming errors and converts them to 500/400

The new wrapping of `loadUsers` in a try/catch that maps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to statusCode 400 and any other error to statusCode 500 masks real bugs (e.g. wrong select shape, missing relations). Also the `if (!Array.isArray(hosts)) throw` is unreachable: `hosts` was already set via `eventType.hosts || []`, so it is always an array. These added checks give a false sense of guarding a code path that cannot fail as written.

teamDestinationCalendars pushed without dedup; can create duplicate events on same calendar

`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` has no de-duplication by `credentialId`/`externalId`. Hosts that share a single connected destination calendar (a common case when multiple members point at the same Google account) will each contribute the same entry, leading EventManager.create to call `createEvent` twice for the same calendar+credential and create duplicate events in that calendar.

updateEvent return is missing externalId/credentialId, breaking editLocation references

`EventResult` now declares `externalId?: string | null` and the `updateLocation` flow in EventManager.ts (lines ~200-211) reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` to build `referencesToCreate`. But `CalendarManager.updateEvent` still returns only `{appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError, calWarnings}` without those two fields. As a result, every references row created by `updateLocation` will have `externalCalendarId: undefined`, losing the link to the underlying calendar event used by `deleteEvent`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes literal 'refresh_token' string into saved credentials

When `refresh_token` is missing from the parsed response the function does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`, mutating the parsed object. Callers then persist this object back into the Credential row (see googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101, office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-273 which spreads tokenResponse.data over o365AuthCredentials). The literal string "refresh_token" is saved as the OAuth refresh token. The next refresh attempt will send that string to Google/Microsoft/etc. and fail, and users have no way to recover without manually editing the DB. true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema's dynamic keys are no-ops in Zod

`z.object({ [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })` does not do what the comments claim. The bracketed expressions are evaluated once at schema creation time and resolve to the string `"ZodString"` (or similar), so this is effectively a single extra key "ZodString" on the object. It does not enforce "any property with a number is the expiry" nor does it allow arbitrary additional properties. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true the schema only requires `access_token` to be a string and otherwise accepts anything, so invalid/garbage token responses from the parent app will pass validation and be written into Cal.com's Credential table.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible types based on sync flag

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, this function calls fetch(...) and returns the fetch Response object. Otherwise it returns whatever refreshFunction() returns (which is provider-specific: a GaxiosResponse for googlecalendar, a HubspotToken for hubspot, an AxiosResponse for zoho-bigin/zohocrm, a fetch Response for office365calendar/office365video/webex/zoomvideo/larkcalendar). Callers then assume the returned value has the same shape as refreshFunction()'s return: e.g. googlecalendar does `res?.data` (GaxiosResponse.data) which is undefined on a fetch Response; hubspot reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` (does not exist on a Response); zoho-bigin reads `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios response shape). Whenever the sync flag is enabled, these integrations will throw at runtime and break OAuth flows. The function must either always return a normalized shape (e.g. parsed JSON) or be split into two functions so callers know which shape they get.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
